headline: 4 four killed in accident while returning from wedding in Chattogram
summary: The victims include the bride's brother and sister, who were traveling to Cox's Bazar after a wedding ceremony in the port city.
details: Four people were killed and seven others injured when a lorry hit a microbus carrying relatives returning from a wedding programme in Karnaphuli upazila, Chattogram.
The accident occurred around 2:00 am on the Chattogram-Cox’s Bazar highway at Patiya-Anwara crossing.
The deceased are Niaz Morshed (22), his sister Mimtah (17), their maternal uncle Md Ferdous Alam (55), and the microbus driver, Md Munna.
The family was returning home to Cox’s Bazar after attending a wedding ceremony at a community centre in the Agrabad area of Chattogram city.
According to the Karnaphuli Police Station officer-in-charge, the lorry hit the microbus while making a high-speed U-turn near the Patiya-Anwara crossing.
Ferdous and Mimtah died on the spot, while two others passed away after being taken to Chattogram Medical College Hospital (CMCH).
Seven other injured passengers were admitted to CMCH, with five of them reported to be in critical condition.
Police have seized the lorry, but the driver and helper have fled the scene.
caption:
A wedding celebration turns into tragedy as 4 people, including the bride's siblings, are killed in a highway crash.

Four people were killed and seven others injured when a lorry hit a microbus carrying relatives returning from a wedding programme in Karnaphuli upazila, Chattogram.

The accident occurred around 2:00 am on the Chattogram-Cox’s Bazar highway at Patiya-Anwara crossing.

The deceased are Niaz Morshed (22), his sister Mimtah (17), their maternal uncle Md Ferdous Alam (55), and the microbus driver, Md Munna.

The family was returning home to Cox’s Bazar after attending a wedding ceremony at a community centre in the Agrabad area of Chattogram city.

According to the Karnaphuli Police Station officer-in-charge, the lorry hit the microbus while making a high-speed U-turn near the Patiya-Anwara crossing.

Ferdous and Mimtah died on the spot, while two others passed away after being taken to Chattogram Medical College Hospital (CMCH).

Seven other injured passengers were admitted to CMCH, with five of them reported to be in critical condition.

Police have seized the lorry, but the driver and helper have fled the scene.

headline_marked: Oil supply fears rise as [[attack on ship in Strait of Hormuz]] reported
headline: Oil supply fears rise as attack on ship in Strait of Hormuz reported
summary: A projectile hit a vessel in the strategic waterway, following the temporary closure of a vital Saudi oil pipeline after a drone attack.
details: The UKMTO reported that a projectile hit a vessel moving through the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday. The extent of the damage and the status of the crew remain unknown.
This incident occurs just after Saudi Arabia temporarily closed its 1,200-km East-West pipeline as a precaution. The closure follows a drone attack that Baghdad and Riyadh say originated in Iraq.
The East-West pipeline is critical, moving 4 to 5 million barrels per day, which accounts for 4% to 5% of the global oil supply.
Brent crude prices have surged back above $100 a barrel, while diesel prices in the US have hit a record $6 a gallon due to ongoing Middle East conflicts.
The Houthis in Yemen have also advanced along the Red Sea and seized the strategic island of Perim in the Bab el-Mandeb strait.
US President Donald Trump has suggested Iran is likely to blame for the pipeline attack, while Saudi Arabia has requested US military help to fight the Houthis.
Iran has stated that dialogue with the US is useless unless all its conditions are met, including recognition of its control over the Strait of Hormuz.
A meeting between Iran and Gulf Arab states is scheduled for Monday in Oman to discuss the future of the the Strait of Hormuz.
caption:

This incident occurs just after Saudi Arabia temporarily closed its 1,200-km East-West pipeline as a precaution. The closure follows a drone attack that Baghdad and Riyadh say originated in Iraq.

The East-West pipeline is critical, moving 4 to 5 million barrels per day, which accounts for 4% to 5% of the global oil supply.

Brent crude prices have surged back above $100 a barrel, while diesel prices in the US have hit a record $6 a gallon due to ongoing Middle East conflicts.

The Houthis in Yemen have also advanced along the Red Sea and seized the strategic island of Perim in the Bab el-Mandeb strait.

US President Donald Trump has suggested Iran is likely to blame for the pipeline attack, while Saudi Arabia has requested US military help to fight the Houthis.

Iran has stated that dialogue with the US is useless unless all its conditions are met, including recognition of its control over the Strait of Hormuz.

A meeting between Iran and Gulf Arab states is scheduled for Monday in Oman to discuss the future of the the Strait of Hormuz.
